description: Weighted audit rules for roadmap contract quality scoring. Each rule is evaluated against a parsed roadmap contract and contributes to a 0-100 maturity score.

changelog.1.1: Added ROADMAP-011 (multiple active releases) and ROADMAP-012 (no active release designated). Status matching is case-insensitive with alias normalization; author lowercase regardless. See ROADMAP_MATURITY_MODEL.md for updated caps.
changelog.1.2: Added the 'detection' block. Detection was previously reimplemented independently by the backend auditor and tools/Test-RoadmapContract.ps1, so the same ROADMAP.md scored differently depending on which tool an operator ran. Detection is now data, not code: both evaluators read these patterns, the release-scoped signal list, and the scoring mode from this file.
changelog.1.3: Moved release-status detection into the 'detection' block as 'releaseStatusPattern' and 'statusVocabulary'. Status was the one signal 1.2 left each evaluator to implement privately: the backend auditor accepted '**Status:** active' and its own in-progress aliases, while Test-RoadmapContract.ps1 required a '> Status:' blockquote and knew no aliases. It was the sole remaining cause of score divergence across the estate, and it drove ROADMAP-011 and ROADMAP-012 -- the two rules that decide whether dispatch has a target -- so a repo with two active releases could read as fully conformant through one tool and be capped at L2 by the other.
changelog.1.4: Two vocabulary corrections surfaced by folding tools/Test-RoadmapStructure.ps1 -- a third private copy of the status contract, missed by 1.3 because it is a structure linter rather than a scorer -- onto this block. (a) 'releaseStatusPattern' now accepts sentence punctuation ('.', ',', ';') as a status terminator alongside end-of-line, dash, and open-paren. The linter had read 'Status: done. Shipped 2026-05.' and 'Status: active, pending review' since it was written; the 1.3 pattern matched neither, so adopting it unchanged would have converted statuses an operator can plainly read into RQ001 'no Status line' warnings. This widens reading only -- authoring tools still emit the canonical '> Status: active' form. The colon became MANDATORY in the same edit: 1.3 wrote it as ':?\**\s*:?' to tolerate both '**Status:**' and '**Status**:', which made a line that merely begins with the word 'status' a status declaration. Harmless while the terminator set was end-of-line, dash, and open-paren; with sentence punctuation added, an ordinary prose sentence starting 'status in one tool and ...' parsed as an unrecognized status. All three documented forms carry a colon, so requiring one costs no real roadmap and makes 1.4 strictly more precise than 1.3, not merely more tolerant. (b) 'productIntentHeadingPattern' accepts 'Product direction'. ROADMAP-004 failed on a repository whose intent section is headed 'Product Direction (summary)', which is a synonym of the already-accepted 'product intent', not a missing section.
changelog.1.5: Demoted ROADMAP-011 from critical to warning, and implemented the two blanket maturity caps ROADMAP_MATURITY_MODEL.md has always documented but no evaluator applied: any critical finding caps maturity at L1, any warning finding caps at L3. The demotion resolves a self-contradiction in the model: ROADMAP-011 carried BOTH a documented L2 cap and critical severity, so applying the blanket critical cap literally would have forced it to L1 and made its own documented L2 cap unreachable. As a warning it takes the L3 blanket cap plus its existing named L2 cap, landing at L2 exactly as documented, and 'any critical finding caps at L1' becomes literally true. Ambiguous dispatch remains a hard gate: L2 is still below the L3 contract-ready bar.

detection.description: Canonical detection contract. Every evaluator of this rule pack MUST derive its signals from these patterns rather than reimplementing them, so that one roadmap file produces one score.
detection.releaseHeadingNote: Depth-tolerant from level 2 down: releases are frequently nested under a numbered parent such as '## 6. Open Releases'. The mandatory dash-and-title suffix keeps prose headings like '### Release 2.0 completion snapshot' from being read as release blocks.
detection.releaseStatusNote: Read inside a release block only; a document-level 'Status:' line above the first release describes the repository, not a dispatch target. Tolerant of the three forms in the estate -- '> Status: active' (the template's canonical form), '**Status:** active', and a bare 'Status: active' -- and of trailing commentary introduced by a dash, an open paren, or sentence punctuation ('Status: done. Shipped 2026-05.', 'Status: active, pending review'). The colon is required, and is the only thing separating a declaration from prose: without it, any line opening with the word 'status' parses as one. Authoring tools must still emit the canonical blockquote form; tolerance applies to reading, never to writing, because an auditor that reports 'no active release' against a file a human can plainly read is worse than one that accepts a second spelling.

statusVocabulary.note: Statuses are matched case-insensitively and normalized through the alias map before any rule reads them. 'activeStatuses' is deliberately just 'active': ROADMAP-011 and ROADMAP-012 exist to identify the single dispatch target, and a blocked or validating release is not one. Widening it would let a roadmap carrying one active plus one blocked release trip the critical single-active-release cap.

detection.productIntentNote: Document-scoped: product intent describes the repository, not a release. A bare 'scope' token is deliberately excluded because it matches the 'Out of scope' heading that every conformant release carries. Synonyms are added on evidence -- 'product direction' entered in 1.4 because a repository in the estate uses it as its intent heading -- not speculatively.
detection.releaseScopedSignalsNote: ROADMAP-006 and ROADMAP-007 read 'at least one RELEASE SECTION includes ...'. A heading found anywhere in the document does not satisfy them; a roadmap with no release sections scores false for both.

meaningfulBody.note: A subsection satisfies its rule only when its body survives this test: strip whitespace and markdown punctuation, require the minimum character count, and reject placeholder text. An empty 'Acceptance criteria' heading is not acceptance criteria.

scoring.note: score = round((sumOfAllRuleWeights - sumOfFailedRuleWeights) / sumOfAllRuleWeights * 100). The rule weights do not sum to 100, so subtracting penalties from a flat 100 produces a different number on the same file and must not be used.

rules.name: roadmap-file-present
rules.description: A ROADMAP.md (or equivalent) file exists in the repository root.
rules.message: No ROADMAP.md file found. The repository has no roadmap at all.
rules.recommendedAction: Create a ROADMAP.md using the canonical template at standards/roadmap/ROADMAP_TEMPLATE.md.

rules.name: roadmap-parseable
rules.description: The roadmap file can be parsed without errors (contains at least one checkbox item).
rules.message: Roadmap file exists but could not be parsed. No checkbox items were found.
rules.recommendedAction: Add at least one release section with checklist items using '- [ ] task' and '- [x] done' syntax.

rules.name: roadmap-has-pending-work
rules.description: The roadmap contains at least one unchecked item, indicating active work.
rules.message: All roadmap items are marked complete. No pending work is visible.
rules.recommendedAction: Add a new release section with future milestones, or archive this roadmap and create a new one.

rules.name: has-product-intent-section
rules.description: The roadmap includes a product intent or scope section that describes what the product does and who it serves.
rules.message: No product intent or scope section detected.
rules.recommendedAction: Add a 'Product Intent' section near the top of ROADMAP.md describing what the product does, who it serves, and the problem it solves.

rules.name: uses-release-sections
rules.description: Work is organized into release-scoped sections (e.g. '## Release X.Y — Title') rather than a single flat list.
rules.message: Roadmap does not use release-scoped sections. Work items appear in a flat or informal structure.
rules.recommendedAction: Reorganize the roadmap into bounded release sections. Each release should have a heading, goal statement, and checklist.

rules.name: has-acceptance-criteria
rules.description: At least one release section includes acceptance criteria defining when the release can be declared done.
rules.message: No acceptance criteria found in any release section.
rules.recommendedAction: Add an 'Acceptance criteria' subsection to each release with observable conditions for completion.

rules.name: has-out-of-scope-boundaries
rules.description: At least one release section explicitly defines what is out of scope.
rules.message: No out-of-scope boundaries found in any release section.
rules.recommendedAction: Add an 'Out of scope' subsection to each release to prevent scope creep and reduce ambiguity for coding agents.

rules.name: sufficient-pending-item-count
rules.description: The roadmap contains enough pending items to justify Copilot dispatch (minimum 3 unchecked items).
rules.message: Fewer than 3 pending roadmap items. The roadmap may not provide sufficient context for reliable dispatch.
rules.recommendedAction: Add more concrete, testable milestones to give Copilot enough bounded work to deliver.

rules.name: has-multiple-releases
rules.description: The roadmap defines more than one release, showing a multi-step plan rather than a single sprint.
rules.message: Only one release section found. A multi-release roadmap provides better forward visibility.
rules.recommendedAction: Add a second release section for the next planned increment of work.

rules.name: no-vague-checklist-items
rules.description: Checklist items are concrete and testable, not vague placeholders.
rules.message: One or more checklist items appear to be vague placeholders.
rules.recommendedAction: Replace vague items with concrete, testable, implementation-specific steps.

rules.name: single-active-release
rules.description: At most one release is marked with normalizedStatus 'active'. A dispatch agent needs one unambiguous execution target.
rules.message: More than one release is marked active. Dispatch target is ambiguous.
rules.recommendedAction: Re-status all but one active release to planned, blocked, validation, or done. Exactly one release should be active at a time.

rules.name: has-designated-active-release
rules.description: When releases exist, exactly one is designated active so dispatch tooling has a default target.
rules.message: Releases exist but none is marked active. Dispatch tooling has no default target.
rules.recommendedAction: Mark the release currently being worked on as 'Status: active'.

L1-Informal.description: Roadmap exists but is a flat list, lacks structure, or has parse errors.

L2-Structured.description: Roadmap has checkboxes and some organization, but lacks release sections, acceptance criteria, or an unambiguous active release.

L3-Contract-Ready.description: Roadmap uses release sections, has acceptance criteria, is parseable, and designates exactly one active release. Ready for supervised dispatch.

L4-Orchestration-Ready.description: Roadmap passes all critical and warning rules. Suitable for autonomous or semi-autonomous Copilot orchestration.
